## Triage: first grade, `tooling` · `priority:p3` · `domain:skills` · `area:devpath`, into `pm:queue`. Maintainer-directed (③), so the queue rule's exemption applies

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-13T01:57Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Queue rule:** a `tooling` card needs `Unblocks:` or a published surface, unless the maintainer directed it. This one carries the maintainer's 「测试遇到的问题，可以提交issue」 verbatim, so it is exempt.
- **Why p3:** each row is a false `fail` against a product that is right. That is noise in the QA run record, not a product defect. Release QA reads these items, so the rows are worth fixing before the next pass.
- **Direction: each row as its table says.** Revise the item, bump `revision`, append `history`, and keep `node scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` green.
  - A2: re-point the three legacy URLs to the Setup metadata catalog. `users` and `organizations` stay.
  - A9: authed 404, anonymous 401, never 2xx. The existing wiring test is the oracle.
  - N5: re-point to the by-invitation rule (the notice with no form; the form only on an accept-invitation redirect or a zero-owner deployment).
  - A3: re-point to the managed-content seal (`403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`). ⛔ No new fixture package built only to reach the R1 gate (new gates default no). If R1 keeps an oracle, it is its unit pins, named in the item.
- Later rows from the same pass are appended here, per the card.
- Triage: lands in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/*.json` (`domain:skills`, the checklist family, as #22987); rationale: test truth.

**Rows added from the same browser pass** · PM seat `domain:devx#2`, `session_016JB93R2KcQP4GgKaUnseVF` · 2026-10-13T02:15Z

| QA-source | disposition | what the clause pins | what the product does, and why that is right |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#23104 · api-backend.formula-stdlib-matrix · C1` (rev 1) | stale spec | 27 advertised stdlib functions; step 1 says to re-count the registration chain and mark the matrix stale if the count moved | `registerStdLib` now registers **29** — the 27 plus `isoDate` and `isoDatetime` (`345d3f3d8`, #22347); `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` lists the same 29, and all 29 pass their known answers against the built `packages/formula/dist` (73/73 rows). Re-count to 29 and add the two rows. Also an assertion defect inside the item: its literal row `joinNonEmpty(['a', null, ' ', 'b'], '-')` cannot evaluate (cel-js refuses a heterogeneous list literal); the same semantics through record fields gives `'a-b'` — rewrite the row that way. |
| `#23104 · api-backend.formula-stdlib-matrix · C6` (rev 1) | stale spec | EXPECTED-FAIL: an unregistered function is a silent null at head | the metadata authoring door now refuses it first: `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/…` adding a field `bad_f = sqrt(4)` → `422 INVALID_METADATA` "… `sqrt` is not a callable name here — a NAME fault …", and nothing is stored (reproduced twice). Flip the clause to the positive authoring-time refusal its own text anticipates. |

| `#23104 · platform-core.keyboard-shortcut-surface · C2` (rev 2) | stale spec | EXPECTED-FAIL K1a: the shortcuts dialog advertises bare `B` while the handler needs ⌘/Ctrl | the dialog advertises `⌘ B` and nothing bare: General — Close dialog/panel `Esc`, Open command palette `⌘ K`, Show keyboard shortcuts `?`; Navigation — Toggle sidebar `⌘ B`. Bare `B` does nothing, `Ctrl+B` toggles — display and binding agree, since objectui#11674 ("the dialog lists only shortcuts whose handler is mounted"). The defect this expected-fail records is gone: flip the clause to the positive assertion. |
| `#23104 · platform-core.keyboard-shortcut-surface · C3` (rev 2) | stale spec | EXPECTED-FAIL K1b: `⌘/`, `N`, `R`, `⌘E`, `⌘D` advertised with no handler | none of the five is advertised any more (same objectui#11674); each still does nothing, measured against its own effect (no search focus, no dialog, no refetch, no edit surface, no theme flip). "Advertised but unwired" no longer exists — revise the clause to assert the advertised set equals the wired set. |
